inputs.original_text: The split comes as some MPs raise the prospect of a new conversation about the party’s leadership Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates Get our breaking news email , free app or daily news podcast Angus Taylor has shut down Andrew Hastie’s push for the Liberals to be “open-minded” to increasing taxes on gas companies and winding back concessions for property investors, exposing a clash of philosophies between the opposition leader and his most likely future rival. The opposition leader also did not repeat Hastie’s criticism of Donald Trump as he refused to say whether or not he endorsed the US and Israel’s war with Iran. Continue reading...
inputs.modified_text: This isn’t just a Liberal leadership spat. It’s about a party choosing to protect tax advantages for gas companies and property investors instead of seriously considering reform—while ordinary people bear the consequences of entrenched wealth. Angus Taylor shutting down Andrew Hastie’s call makes those priorities hard to miss. And on the US and Israel’s war with Iran, Taylor wouldn’t say whether he supported it or repeat Hastie’s criticism of Donald Trump. The public deserves leaders who are clear about military force and willing to challenge powerful interests at home.
